notes.text: This sheet is a computer printout with blue handwritten annotations. The print and blue notes are upside down in the supplied scan; the pencil 33 has the opposite orientation. The original was viewed once. Each existing native half was then rotated losslessly by 180 degrees, without rescaling, for its first and only detailed view. The three subsequent tight crops were also rotated by 180 degrees after extraction from their recorded original-image boxes.

The print has three initial rows of asterisks and a visible 0.0000, followed by 75.000 and 62 rows of three decimal values. The first column runs from 0.0307 to 0.0389. Every number, sign and decimal point was read against C, including the sign transition at the 0.0333/0.0334 rows and the -1.0000 value at 0.0366. No numeric correction to C was found. The source does not name the columns.

The blue max annotation has a closing-parenthesis guide across both printed 39.1337 values, on rows 0.0347 and 0.0349. The separate blue statements read ΔU=26.3878 and U_m=25.939, each followed by the unresolved m/s|m/o unit string. The shortened 25.939 is kept even though the separate addition stack ends at 25.9398.

The first arithmetic stack writes 39.1337 above 12.7459, a rule, and 26.3878. The second writes 12.7459 above 13.1939, a rule, and 25.9398. No operator signs occur beside either stack, so none are supplied. A narrow decimal subtraction check was used only to corroborate the ambiguous-looking first post-decimal digit in the first stack; it did not substitute calculated text for the visible numerals.

The candidate retains C’s transcription and its order of the separate annotation blocks. The inventory records their physical positions to the right of the table. The printer producer and the blue and pencil writers are not identified by evidence on this page. Paper folds, holes and isolated background specks are not transcribed as source writing.

The main reader inspected the original orientation and all three existing crops. The first post-decimal digit of the first stack is a short upright with a left entry stroke; the final 7 has a broader curved top and transverse stroke. The numerical check corroborates the preferred 1 but does not supply unseen digits. The list inventory category denotes this computer-produced numerical sheet, not an attribution to the notebook author.
